subject: Codex Design on PickAPlugin
text:
Hi,

I came across Codex Design and the canvas idea is really nice, especially being able to click an element in a mockup and tweak it right there. I run PickAPlugin, a small hand-sorted directory of Codex and ChatGPT plugins, and I'd like to add it as a free listing (pointing to ummydev/codexdesign with your install steps). Is that ok with you?

Once it's up you can also grab a free README badge that links to the listing, and if you ever mention plugin directories on codexdesign.io, a link back to https://pickaplugin.com would be appreciated. No pressure either way.

Aaron, PickAPlugin

subject: Your Codex plugins install guide
text:
Hi,

I read your Codex plugins post from Nov 5. The step by step for /plugins and the marketplace add forms is one of the clearer write-ups I've seen. I run PickAPlugin, a directory of Codex plugins, and we have a free install command finder (paste a GitHub repo, get the install line from its README or the standard marketplace add command): https://pickaplugin.com/tools/plugin-install-command

If you think it fits next to your "Add a marketplace from the CLI" section, a link would be great. We also have a free-to-cite data report on Codex plugins if you ever need numbers: https://pickaplugin.com/research/state-of-codex-plugins-2026

Aaron, PickAPlugin

subject: One more for your MCP directories list
text:
Hi,

Your list of 48 MCP marketplaces and directories is really thorough, I like that each entry says what to prepare. Would you consider adding PickAPlugin? It's a free, hand-sorted directory of Codex and ChatGPT plugins, and that includes plugins that bundle MCP servers. Makers submit a GitHub repo here, no fee: https://pickaplugin.com/submit

We're still small, so I won't pretend we send big traffic, but it's a good fit for anyone shipping their MCP server as a Codex plugin.

Aaron, PickAPlugin

subject: Your where to submit an MCP server guide
text:
Hi,

I liked your where to submit an MCP server guide, the table with what each site actually needs and what it costs saves people a lot of clicking. Could PickAPlugin go in there? We're a free, hand-sorted directory of Codex and ChatGPT plugins, and MCP servers packaged as plugins are welcome. Submitting is just a public GitHub repo, free: https://pickaplugin.com/submit

We also keep a similar list on our side (https://pickaplugin.com/guides/where-to-submit-mcp-server), so happy to look at adding Plug and Ship there too.

Aaron, PickAPlugin

subject: Your best MCP directories field guide
text:
Hi,

I read your Nov 5 piece on MCP server directories. I appreciated the upfront note that you run one of the sites, we do the same thing on our pages. I run PickAPlugin, a hand-sorted directory of Codex and ChatGPT plugins, a lot of which bundle MCP servers.

If you ever expand the list with a line for people working in Codex, we'd be glad to be in it: https://pickaplugin.com. And if you need numbers on the Codex side, our research is free to cite: https://pickaplugin.com/research/state-of-codex-plugins-2026

Aaron, PickAPlugin

subject: A link for The Queue maybe
text:
Hi,

I like the three-issue format, especially Friday's Queue with a line on why each link is worth it. I run PickAPlugin, a small directory of Codex and ChatGPT plugins, and we put together a data report on the community plugin ecosystem (licenses, install commands, how many want API keys, that kind of thing): https://pickaplugin.com/research/state-of-codex-plugins-2026

It's free to cite with a credit link if it's ever useful for an issue. A lot of these plugins ship as MCP servers too, so it might fit your readers.

Aaron, PickAPlugin
